A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deterministic Differentiable Pruning (DDP) work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning experiments, component and data ablations, learned sparsity analyses, and measured inference speedups in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds recovery-budget experiments, additional baseline comparisons, training-cost measurements, and learned-mask distributions.

M1.justification: The ReLU forward masks, annealed retention surrogate, sparsity and binarization objectives, distillation, MoE extension, and group-level sparsity formulation remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same algorithm; revised experimental hyperparameters do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training and evaluation coverage: FineWeb-Edu, C4, LaMini, WikiText-2, the downstream benchmark suite, and ShareGPT prompts. V2 adds model checkpoints and pruning configurations, without adding datasets, tasks, or input-environment scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives: Table 8 introduces Týr-the-Pruner, Table 7 adds HEAPr with LoRA recovery and extends the existing LoRAP recovery comparison, and Table 9 compares training costs against LoRA and full fine-tuning. The original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include recovery budgets up to 120M tokens, additional LLaMA-2 and Mistral checkpoints, 12.5/25/37.5% pruning settings, and controlled training-cost profiling. Appendix C also changes the reported lambda2 learning rate from 0.8 throughout to 0.4 at 20% sparsity and 0.8 at higher sparsity, and restricts the eta=2 statement to 20% sparsity. These reporting revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted analyses of whether longer LoRA recovery compensates for pruning decisions, the training overhead of distillation, and whether learned masks exploit continuous rescaling (Figure 7). Existing component, granularity, token-budget, dataset, and sparsity-pattern analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new mask histograms describe variation across components, rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results in Tables 7–9 and Figure 7 while retaining the original benchmark values. For example, Table 7 reports 62.98 accuracy for LoRAP with 120M recovery tokens versus DDP's retained 64.82 at 30M tokens; Table 9 adds training-cost measurements. Section 5.1 also revises reported run times from approximately 20 to 40 minutes for LLaMA-7B and 40 to 60 minutes for DeepSeekMoE-16B. Added results should not be interpreted as same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The theoretical assumptions, propositions, theorems, and proofs remain substantively unchanged. Proposition B.2 corrects the recalled budget symbol from T to P, aligning it with Equation (21); this repairs notation without changing the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: deterministic mask-only pruning, expanded mask expressivity, improved optimization and pruning quality, applicability to dense and MoE models, and practical inference speedups.

C2.justification: V2 newly interprets limited LoRA recovery as evidence that initial sparse structure is a bottleneck because recovery cannot revise pruning decisions. It also interprets mask distributions as evidence of component rescaling and explains training overhead through adapter computations and the teacher forward pass.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository hyperlink and public-availability statement. It revises training-time estimates and Appendix C hyperparameters, and documents the new cost comparison's rank-8 LoRA, per-device batch size, gradient accumulation, and activation checkpointing. Higher-sparsity distillation coefficients remain unspecified after narrowing the eta=2 statement.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Týr-the-Pruner reference and positions DDP against it experimentally in Section 5.6. The related-work taxonomy and existing novelty framing remain unchanged; HEAPr's citation-year suffix changes only to disambiguate references.

P1.justification: V2 inserts sections on LoRA recovery, additional comparisons, and computational cost, and expands the mask-analysis discussion. It also clarifies latent-parameter terminology, fixes grammar and notation, and updates publication, funding, and conflict-of-interest text. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables and a three-panel mask-distribution figure. Existing speedup and appendix tables are renumbered, and appendix tables and sparsity figures are redistributed across pages. Existing visual content and the overall presentation style are retained.

improvement.justification: The added recovery and training-cost comparisons provide more direct evidence for DDP's practical advantages, while the code link and implementation details improve reproducibility information. However, unexplained discrepancies limit the benefit: for LLaMA-2-7B at 50% sparsity, retained Table 2 reports WikiText-2 perplexity 26.34, whereas new Table 8 reports 10.34 without explaining a setting difference. The useful additional evidence supports a modest overall improvement, rather than a substantial strengthening of the paper.
